newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tea industry sees 1996 output at 775 mln kg.
newsitem.headline: Indian tea industry sees 1996 output at 775 mln kg.

text.p: India is forecast to produce 775 million kg of tea in 1996, up sharply from 754 million the previous year, industry officials and traders said on Friday.
"The crop is up. The outlook is bright," said R.K. Krishna Kumar, chairman of the Consultative Committee of Plantation Associations, a tea planters body.
"The output in calendar 1996 is expected to be 775 million kg against 754 last year," Kumar told Reuters.
He said tea exports in 1996 were expected to rise to 170 million kg from the previous year's 164 million.

"India is looking into the Pakistan market, which is the world's second largest importer. We are hopeful of striking a deal with Pakistani importers soon," said V. Ramaswamy, an official with leading auctioners Carritt Moran.
Ramaswamy said the export market would grow once Russia increased tea purchases from India, and Indian tea entered the Pakistan market.
Each year Russia buys 60 million kg from India. The fromer Soviet Union used to import around 100 million kgs every year.
India exports tea to the other members of the Confederation of Independent States, Poland, the United States, Canada, Egypt, Iran and the European Union.
Kumar said the tea industry was very optimistic that annual production would rise to 1.08 billion kg by 2006.
India will have 255 million kgs of tea for export in 2006 after meeting domestic demand, he said.

"Russia is currently buying more tea from Sri Lanka despite an increase in their prices because it (Sri Lanka) is offering longer term credit," Ramaswamy said. "This particularly affects the south Indian market."
Officials said the south Indian tea industry was appealing to the government for better credit norms to make Indian tea prices more competitive.
Traders said tea prices at domestic auction centres averaged 40 rupees a kg, but they were hopeful prices would rise to between 45 and 50 rupees a kg before the end of the year.

Some 75 percent of the country's tea is produced in the northeastern states of Assam, Meghalaya and Tripura, and Darjeeling in West Bengal state. The remaining 25 percent is grown in the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
